The latest Bloomberg report points out that the new CEO, John Ternus, is planning a "comprehensive overhaul" of Apple, aiming to make the company "faster and leaner." Reform measures include launching more products, streamlining "mid-level management positions," and various other adjustments.

John Ternus is determined to reshape Apple. Here is an overview of his reform agenda.

First, the new Apple CEO hopes to accelerate the rollout of more products, including ones that are "more experimental." One idea is to break Apple's spring and fall product release cadence, distributing new product launches more evenly throughout the year.

Ternus also hopes to "build a leaner, more engineer-driven organisational structure," involving multiple cost-cutting measures and restructuring. One of the changes is to "streamline some mid-level management positions so engineers are closer to senior management."

The report points out that over the past two weeks, Apple has laid off "a number of Engineering Project Managers (EPMs)" from the hardware engineering division. Bloomberg describes these positions as having long been "central to Apple's product development process," responsible for "managing schedules and coordinating work between teams."

The report stated: "Those affected include a number of project managers, among them about six directors, who are among the company's most senior employees. These employees have only been given a few weeks to find other positions within the company, or they will face being laid off later this year."

Bloomberg noted that the related cost-cutting measures could expand further. In fact, Ternus has long argued over the years that Apple should become more "lean":

In addition, it is reported that Apple has shelved a plan to cut 5,000 AppleCare employees this summer, believing that AI agents can handle the related work.

At the same time, Ternus hopes to collaborate with Eddy Cue and Chief Financial Officer Kevan Parekh to drive growth in Apple's services business revenue. The report stated: "They have discussed launching new services and exploring more revenue from existing products and businesses."
